title: Algorithmic monoculture in model adoption across farms
setting: Nine synthetic model families with different predictive risks make correlated recommendation errors across 1000 farms. Each error is a model-common shock (share rho=0.25, with cross-model correlation kappa) plus a farm-specific error. Each farm adopts one model, and the allocation rule sets adoption shares: the best-risk model for all farms, a uniform split, or a convex portfolio that minimizes modeled social loss subject to an average private-regret cap. Risks are estimated from a noisy benchmark, and social loss (private squared error plus a quadratic penalty on the aggregate error, lambda=20) is measured on fresh simulated error draws.

paper.title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation
paper.claim: A regret-capped diversified adoption portfolio lowers social loss relative to accuracy-driven monoculture, but correlated errors across models attenuate the benefit, and uniform allocation can breach the regret cap.

metric.name: social_loss
metric.description: Mean social loss on fresh error draws: 0.5 * mean squared (normalized) farm error plus 0.5 * lambda * squared norm of the across-farm mean error. Lower is better. Diagnostics: private_loss, system_loss, regret (average private regret relative to the true best model), cap_ok (1 if regret is within the cap).

factors.name: method
factors.description: Adoption rule: all farms use the model with the lowest estimated risk; a regret-capped loss-minimizing convex portfolio (paper method); or equal shares across all nine models.

factors.name: kappa
factors.description: Pairwise correlation between model-common shocks of different model families.

factors.name: gap
factors.description: Spread of true model risks relative to the best model: small means the other models are within about 8% of the best risk, large means up to about 2x.

factors.name: cap
factors.description: Allowed average private regret (delta) of the portfolio relative to the best estimated model's risk.
